accuracy.evidence: Matches KS2 life-cycle diagram skill: butterfly egg→larva→pupa→adult; frog spawn→tadpole→froglet→adult; plant seed→seedling→plant→flower (then seeds). Circular layout with arrows because offspring restart the stages. Aligns with NC Y5 Living things (life cycles of insect, amphibian, plant reproduction) while staying diagram-focused for ages 7–8.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets wrong order (adult before larva), skipping pupa, thinking the cycle ends at adult, mixing frog and butterfly stages, and omitting the return arrow. Challenge why() covers egg/spawn/pup/tad/none/old/rand.

lab_distinct.evidence: flagcycle places stages on a circle, adds arrows to close the loop, and fixes a broken diagram. flagseed is about growing a seed; flagbaby is animals and babies. This lab is specifically the circular diagram with ordered stages.

lab_teaches.evidence: Building three cycles then fixing a wrong stage makes the child use order and the return arrow. Show-me places stages then arrows; live labels read progress.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions: after caterpillar → pupa; spawn → tadpoles; plant starts at seed; egg→adult→pupa→larva is wrong because order is broken.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Seven challenge items with tagged wrongs and specific feedback naming larva/pupa mix-ups, missing return arrows, and plant vs animal stages.

readability.evidence: Kid sentences are short for ages 7–8 with exact terms larva/pupa/spawn/froglet introduced in brackets. Adult stays clear and curriculum-tied.

no_filler.evidence: No banned filler phrases. Each paragraph teaches a cycle or the diagram rule.

mobile.evidence: young class, large circular slots, lbtn twins for every place/arrow/fix action, usable at 390px.

accessibility.evidence: Button twins; canvas aria-label via say(); challenge buttons with aria-live status.

sources: National Curriculum in England: science — Year 5 Living things and their habitats (life cycles of mammal, amphibian, insect, bird; reproduction in plants and animals)
Year 2 animals including humans (offspring) as prior
